blogs.title: When Third‑Party Marks Discern Brand Power — Rethinking DuPont Factor Six
blogs.description: This post dissects the Court’s vacatur of TTB’s restrictive view that only credit‑card–specific third‑party uses matter under DuPont factor 6, arguing instead that the standard encompasses all ‘similar’ goods/services already established under fact‑finding from factor 2. It examines doctrinal ramifications for fintech trademark disputes where a single word like ‘Aspire’ surfaces across varied financial products.

blogs.title:
Credit Cards Are Banks? Reexamining Service Definitions After Apex v.
CC Serve
blogs.description: Here we review how the Board applied federal trademark categories—credit‑card services versus banking & financing—and investigate why the Court ultimately affirmed its conclusion that these services are legally intertwined enough for confusion assessment purposes. The piece explores consequences for applicants who attempt to skirt strong prior marks by narrowly framing their intended goods.

blogs.title: Lost Hashtags Study – Understanding Commercial Strength Through Third‑Party Use
blogs.description: This article explores the Court’s finding that a mark cannot be deemed weak solely from lackluster third‑party activity when contrasted against a theoretically strong prior user whose own mark has resisted dilution attempts via similar use cases—a nuance critical when challengers rely on weak‑mark defenses amid crowded markets.

blogs.title: De Novo Meets Substantial Evidence In Trademark Appeals — A Rules Primer
blogs.description:
A practical guide summarizing why Fed Circuit reviews Board technical conclusions anew while preserving factual determinations only if supported by substantial evidence—and why this split standard predicted both affirmation and remand outcomes in Apex v.
CC Serve.
